L1.title: Constitution: Assembly
L1.intent: All Legislators vote. Ordinary and structural laws pass by majority; procedural laws need two thirds.
L1.author: constitution

L2.title: L2 Currency: Crown (Reserve-backed, Legislator-minted)
L2.intent: Create a stable, reserve-backed currency to enable fair trade, reduce barter friction, and build public trust in exchange. The reserve grows from voluntary public contributions; Legislators vote to control mint supply; each Crown is redeemable for reserve items at a fixed rate. Promotes transparent, fair commerce and reduces friction in economic life.
L2.author: Bruna

patches.reason: Diff: the old create_currency call was gated on round()==2, which never fired after enactment, so it never ran. I moved it into on_enact, and added a once-only on_round_start fallback (guarded by state['crown_made']) because the law is already enacted. Nothing else changed. Mint and redeem rules are left to a Legislator law, since the original code had none.

L3.title: Bribery Disclosure
L3.intent: Every transfer to a Legislator, Board member or the Fixer is published.
L3.code:
title = 'Bribery Disclosure'
intent = 'Every transfer to a Legislator, Board member or the Fixer is published.'

def on_transfer(src,dst,item,qty):
  r=rights_of(dst)
  if 'vote' in r or 'veto' in r or 'fix' in r or 'propose' in r:
    gazette(src+' transferred '+str(qty)+' '+item+' to '+dst)
  return 0
L3.author: Abel

L4.title: Broad Franchise
L4.intent: All agents of J0 vote on ordinary laws by simple majority; no new veto or agenda powers.
L4.author: Abel

patches.reason: Fix requested by Cass (r27). DIFF: kept the ordinary procedure unchanged (electorate = all J0 members, simple majority, closes in 1). ADDED give(), which grants 'propose' and 'vote' to any member lacking them; it is called in on_enact and on_round_start. WHY: every Legislator has left, so no member holds propose, and the franchise L4 exists to give is empty. This is the smallest change that lets members take part in ordinary lawmaking again. It adds no veto, no agenda control, no fees.
patches.diff:
--- L4 (before)
+++ L4 (after)
@@ -1,8 +1,19 @@
-title = 'Broad Franchise'
-intent = 'All agents of J0 vote on ordinary laws by simple majority; no new veto or agenda powers.'
+title = "Broad Franchise"
+intent = "Every member of J0 may propose and vote on ordinary laws, which pass by simple majority of all members."
 
 def ordinary_proc(p):
-  return {'electorate': members(), 'rule': 'majority', 'closes_in': 1}
+    return {"electorate": members(), "rule": "majority", "closes_in": 1}
+
+def give():
+    for a in members():
+        if not has(a, 'propose'):
+            grant(a, 'propose')
+        if not has(a, 'vote'):
+            grant(a, 'vote')
 
 def on_enact():
-  set_procedure('ordinary', ordinary_proc)
+    set_procedure('ordinary', ordinary_proc)
+    give()
+
+def on_round_start(r):
+    give()

L9.title: Tribute T2 Reserve Payment
L9.intent: Pay Tribute T2 from the Commonwealth reserve on enact. This is an ordinary law filed well before the T2 deadline to ensure the reserve payment executes before the due date, avoiding the procedural veto-window trap that delayed L6 in T1.

L10.title: T2 Reserve Payment
L10.intent: Pay the open tribute demand from the reserve, capped at the amount due and at reserve holdings. No mint, no procedure change.
L10.author: Abel

patches.code:
title = "T2 Reserve Payment"
intent = "Pay Tribute T2 from the reserve, capped at the amount due."
CAP = 200
def on_enact():
    left = CAP
    r = reserve()
    for item in ["timber", "stone", "silver"]:
        have = r.get(item, 0)
        v = value(item)
        if left <= 0 or v <= 0 or have <= 0:
            continue
        q = min(have, left / v)
        pay_tribute(item, q)
        left = left - q * v
patches.reason: DIFF: on_enact used to call pay_tribute(item, have) for every reserve item, which pays the whole reserve (about 573 value). Now it pays timber, then stone, then silver, up to a total value of CAP=200 (min(have, left/value) per item). WHY: the intent and comment say 'capped at the amount due'. No law function reads the demand, so the cap is hard-coded. It is set well above T1's 75.9 to allow for growth, so T2 is still paid in full and the reserve is not drained.

patches.reason: DIFF: the payment loop now sits in pay(). It runs once (guarded by state['paid']) from on_enact, on_round_start and on_round_end, and CAP goes from 200 to 131. WHY: L10 was enacted in r20, before T2 was demanded at the start of r21, so on_enact had nothing to pay and the reserve never moved (258 timber, 197 stone, 7.4 silver).
